paper_metadata.title: Semi-supervised Generative Open Information Extraction
paper_metadata.venue: Nanyang Technological University, Master of Engineering thesis
paper_metadata.abstract: OpenIE extracts n-ary relation tuples from unstructured text without a predefined ontology. This thesis surveys neural OpenIE and proposes a mean-teacher semi-supervised generative OpenIE method: a jointly prompted extraction/verification model learns from labelled data and verified pseudo-labels from unlabeled text. It also reports exploratory zero-shot ChatGPT experiments.

problem_addressed: Improve generative OpenIE when high-quality labelled training data are scarce and bootstrapped labels are noisy or unsuitable for differing application-specific annotation preferences. The objective is to exploit unlabeled Wikipedia text while filtering unreliable pseudo-extractions.

methodology.description: The proposed Semi-supervised UIE-OIE is a T5-small-based generative OpenIE system. It first jointly pre-trains extraction and pseudo-label-verification tasks using task prompts. Extraction maps a sentence directly to a UIE-inspired tree sequence in which each predicate is a relation node with subject/object argument leaves; no schema sequence is supplied because OpenIE is schema-free. Verification maps a sentence plus one tree-form extraction to true/false. Negative verification examples are synthesized by mismatching subject–predicate pairs across tuples, swapping subject and object, and extending an object with remaining sentence text. In semi-supervised training, identically initialized student and EMA mean-teacher models are used. For unlabeled sentences, the teacher greedily generates trees; malformed outputs are removed, candidates are filtered by a perplexity threshold, and each extraction is verified. The student trains on gold labels plus retained pseudo-labels with supervised, consistency, and R-Drop symmetric-KL regularization losses; the teacher is updated by EMA. Verification and extraction examples are balanced by random sampling.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: No predefined ontology or extraction schema is used. The method explicitly removes UIE's schema sequence from the input for OpenIE; output roles are generic relation, subject, object, and object2 labels rather than an ontology.

input_output.input_type: English unstructured natural-language sentences; training additionally uses a prompted sentence plus a candidate tree-form extraction for the verification task.
input_output.output_representation: A concatenated, tree-based text sequence of zero or more open n-ary tuples: every tree has a predicate/root labelled relation and argument leaves labelled subject, object, object2, etc. For verification, the output is the single token true or false.

models_and_tools: Mean-teacher student/teacher models with exponential moving average
datasets: LSOIE-wiki: QA-SRL 2.0-derived Wikipedia OpenIE data; 19,676 training sentences/46,015 tuples and 2,403 test sentences/5,374 tuples

CaRB: crowd-sourced Newswire and Wikipedia evaluation data; rule-based OpenIE4 pseudo-labels used for the 92,774-sentence/190,661-tuple training set and 634 test sentences/2,701 tuples in the reported table
76,043 unlabeled Wikipedia sentences collected from English Wikidump

baselines: UIE-OIE augmented with pseudo-labels generated from unlabeled text
evaluation.setting: Experiments evaluate LSOIE-wiki and CaRB under CaRB (1-1) scoring. The base model is first trained under full supervision, then initializes student and teacher for semi-supervised learning. For CaRB, rule-generated OpenIE4 labels are used for training because the benchmark itself is insufficient to train a deep model. T5-small experiments use batch size 32, max input/output lengths 256, initial learning rate 5e-5, AdamW with a linear schedule and 6% warm-up; semi-supervised stage lasts 5 epochs for CaRB and 10 for LSOIE variants. Thresholds are 0.1 for perplexity and 0.95 for verification.

value: On LSOIE-wiki, UIE-OIE with verification achieved F1 70.1 and AUC 55.1, above UIE-OIE without semi-supervision (68.2/52.7), IMoJIE (65.3/49.0), IGL-OIE (61.7/45.1), and the no-verification semi-supervised variant (69.4/54.2).

On CaRB, the no-verification semi-supervised variant was best among proposed variants at F1 42.8 and AUC 25.1; adding verification scored 42.1/24.7, whereas UIE-OIE scored 41.8/23.5 and augmentation 42.0/24.0.

Ablation on LSOIE-wiki: consistency loss raised F1 from 68.2 to 68.6; adding self-regularization reached 69.4. All negative-example strategies together yielded 70.11 versus 69.4 base; a separate verifier reached 69.5 versus 70.1 for the joint model.
Tree output outperformed tuple-sequence output (LSOIE-wiki F1 68.2 vs 64.7; CaRB 41.8 vs 41.1). T5-base slightly underperformed T5-small (LSOIE-wiki 68.0 vs 68.2; CaRB 41.5 vs 41.8).

Review-level inference: The reported gains are benchmark-specific and cannot establish general superiority because annotation noise and divergent annotation specifications materially affect scores.
